catalog_quote: 2.5 Stress. Stress in Amari is not phonemic. In general, the first syllable of a two-syllable word is stressed, and in words of more than two syllables, the first syllable is stressed, and then every alternate syllable is stressed. Slightly heavier stress falls on the first syllable. e.g. sàgat woman, ì-saŋʔ is enough, màmu cassowary, màragàmp white, bìŋan-gàŋʔ my name, gàdugàdu type of banana, Bùsuŋàwa woman's name, ŋàrubìni good.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (90 pp offprint, sealang.net CC BY-SA online edition of Pacific Linguistics A-70:77-166; the PDF's metadata gives the title 'A morphology and grammar of Adzera (Amari dialect)..', author Susanne Holzknecht). Locator confirmed: PDF page 18 = printed p. 94, header 'SUSANNE HOLZKNECHT', section '2.5 Stress' (text lines 951-955 of). I rendered the page scan and read it directly. The prose is verbatim as quoted: 'Stress in Amari is not phonemic. In general, the first syllable of a two-syllable word is stressed, and in words of more than two syllables, the first syllable is stressed, and then every alternate syllable is stressed. Slightly heavier stress falls on the first syllable.'…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-contrastive word stress: primary stress on the word-initial syllable; in words of three or more syllables, rhythmic secondary stress on every second syllable after the first (odd-numbered syllables counting from the left), with the initial syllable carrying the heaviest stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Alternating: every alternate syllable after the stressed first syllable is stressed, with the first syllable slightly heavier (i.e. primary initial, secondaries on syllables 3, 5..).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; hedged with 'In general'. Examples include a prefixed verb (i-saŋʔ) and a suffixed noun (biŋan-gaŋʔ) treated under the same rule, but no explicit discussion of affixes or exceptions.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, stated for citation forms of the Amari dialect; stress explicitly 'not phonemic'. Intonation (declarative fall, interrogative rise-fall on last syllable) is treated separately in section 2.6.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is for the Amari dialect of Adzera (S. Holzknecht 1986 title: 'Amari dialect'; Amari is one of six Adzera dialect areas per Holzknecht 1989 Table 4.3, a three-vowel dialect lacking the o/u contrast). Glottolog 5.1 lists no separate dialect glottocode under adze1240, so it maps to adze1240 itself. K. Holzknecht 1973 (no stress data) describes the Central/Kaiapit-Sangang norm.

sources.note: Section 2.5 Stress (p. 94): stress not phonemic; first syllable stressed in disyllables; in longer words first syllable stressed and every alternate syllable thereafter, slightly heavier stress on the first syllable. Examples listed (sagat, mamu, maragamp, gadugadu, Busungawa, ngarubini). Section 2.6 covers intonation.
